issues.description: The problem statement asks students to implement a function named `_construct_zero_state_prep_circuit(...)` (leading underscore) but both the provided template and the reference solution define and use `construct_zero_state_prep_circuit(...)` (no leading underscore). This name mismatch between the problem text and the codebase can confuse students about which symbol to implement and may cause automated tests (or students' attempts) to fail if they follow the problem text verbatim.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the function name consistent across artifacts. Either (A) update the problem statement to request `construct_zero_state_prep_circuit(...)` (no leading underscore), or (B) add a thin wrapper function named `_construct_zero_state_prep_circuit(...)` in the template that delegates to `construct_zero_state_prep_circuit(...)`. Ensure tests and examples reference the same name.

issues.description: The problem statement names the state-preparation function _construct_zero_state_prep_circuit (with a leading underscore), while both the template and the solution define and implement construct_zero_state_prep_circuit (no leading underscore). This mismatch can confuse students about which function name to implement or call and may cause test harness failures or unnecessary search for a differently named stub.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single consistent name across all artifacts. Rename the function in the problem statement to construct_zero_state_prep_circuit (remove the leading underscore) to match the template and solution, or alternatively rename the template/solution functions to _construct_zero_state_prep_circuit if the leading underscore is intentional.
